Class RuleBasedImplicitCallModel

java.lang.Object
sootup.callgraph.implicit.RuleBasedImplicitCallModel
All Implemented Interfaces:
ImplicitCallModel
public class RuleBasedImplicitCallModel extends Object implements ImplicitCallModel
An ImplicitCallModel defined by ImplicitCall rules.

A call with the subsignature of a rule's source fires the rule if the analysis would not see the implicit call otherwise. The call is resolved with the ImplicitCallContext's method lookup; it must resolve to the source, or the class that it names must be a subtype of the source's class. Then:

  • A virtual or interface call fires the rule if one of the methods that the analysis dispatches it to (ImplicitCallContext.callTargets(MethodSignature, InvokableStmt)) is the source, e.g. Thread.start(), whose body calls run() only through the virtual machine, or is an implementation of the source that the analysis does not follow, e.g. the execute(Runnable) of a library Executor. An implementation that it follows shows what it does itself. Which receivers the analysis considers, and so which targets, depends on the analysis: CHA dispatches a call that names Thread to Thread.start(), a points-to analysis that knows the receiver is a subclass that overrides start() does not. If the analysis does not give the targets, the resolved method stands for them.
  • A super or static call fires the rule if it resolves to the source, or to an implementation that the analysis does not follow.
  • A call that does not resolve fires the rule if it names the source's class, or a class in the view that is a subtype of it. A call that names another class that is not in the view does not: whether that class implements the source is unknown.

An implicit invocation names the class in which its method is looked up: the target's ImplicitCallTarget.Direct.declaringClass(), or else the type that the call gives the value, i.e. the parameter type for an argument and the class that the call names for the receiver. The static type of the value's local replaces it if it is a subtype, so that a local typed more precisely narrows the dispatch, while a local typed more widely, e.g. Object for a value passed to an interface parameter, does not lose the call.

    • resolve

      public @NonNull List<AbstractInstanceInvokeExpr> resolve(@NonNull ImplicitCallContext context, @NonNull Body body, @NonNull InvokableStmt stmt)
      Description copied from interface: ImplicitCallModel
      Returns the invocations that the given call statement performs implicitly. Each invocation calls a method on a local of the given body; its arguments are the values that the implicitly called method receives, or NullConstant for parameters without a value.
      Specified by:
      resolve in interface ImplicitCallModel
      Parameters:
      context - the lookup and the analyzed methods of the analysis
      body - the body that contains the statement
      stmt - the call statement
      Returns:
      the implicit invocations, empty if there are none
